title: Atomic Structure

notes.heading: 1. Bohr Model, Hydrogenic Radii/Energies & Rydberg Spectral Lines
notes.proseLatex: For one-electron hydrogenic species ($\text{H}, \text{He}^+, \text{Li}^{2+}$) of atomic number $Z$, angular momentum is quantized as $mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$, giving orbit radius $r_n = 0.529\,\frac{n^2}{Z}\text{ \AA}$, speed $v_n \propto \frac{Z}{n}$, and total energy $E_n = -13.6\,\frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ eV}$ (with $K = -E$ and $U = 2E$). Transitions from $n_2 \to n_1$ emit wavenumbers $\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$ across Lyman ($n_1=1$, UV), Balmer ($n_1=2$, visible), and Paschen ($n_1=3$, IR), producing up to $\frac{\Delta n(\Delta n+1)}{2}$ distinct spectral lines.

keyFormulas.label: Bohr Radius, Energy & Rydberg Formula
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Scale Bohr radius/energy for H, He+, Li2+ and identify spectral series.

examples.problemLatex: Calculate the ionization energy (from ground state $n=1$ to $\infty$) of singly ionized helium $\text{He}^+$ ($Z = 2$).

notes.heading: 2. Quantum Numbers (n, l, m, s), Nodes & Heisenberg Uncertainty
notes.proseLatex: Four quantum numbers specify every orbital electron: principal $n = 1,2,3,\dots$, azimuthal $l = 0,\dots,n-1$ ($s,p,d,f$), magnetic $m_l = -l,\dots,+l$ ($2l+1$ orbitals per subshell; $n^2$ orbitals and $2n^2$ max electrons per shell), and spin $m_s = \pm\frac{1}{2}$. Any $(n,l)$ orbital has $l$ angular nodes and $(n - l - 1)$ radial nodes ($n - 1$ total nodes). Heisenberg's uncertainty principle demands $\Delta x\cdot\Delta p_x \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$.

keyFormulas.label: Subshell Capacity, Node Counts & Heisenberg Limit
keyFormulas.latex: $\text{Radial nodes} = n - l - 1,\quad \text{Angular nodes} = l,\quad e^-_{\max,\text{shell}} = 2n^2,\quad \Delta x\,\Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Validate allowed (n, l, m_l, m_s) tuples and count radial/angular nodes.

examples.problemLatex: How many radial nodes and angular nodes are present in a $4d$ orbital?
stepsLatex: Angular nodes $= l = 2$; radial nodes $= n - l - 1 = 4 - 2 - 1 = 1$ (total nodes $= 3$).

notes.heading: 3. Aufbau (n + l) Rule, Pauli Exclusion, Hund's Rule & Cr/Cu Exceptions
notes.proseLatex: Subshells fill in increasing $(n + l)$ order (lower $n$ wins ties, e.g., $4s$ [$4+0=4$] fills before $3d$ [$3+2=5$]). Pauli forbids two electrons sharing all four quantum numbers, while Hund's rule maximizes parallel spins in degenerate orbitals with spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM}$ ($n =$ unpaired electrons). Half-filled and fully-filled exchange stability gives $\text{Cr}$ ($Z=24$): $[\text{Ar}]\,3d^5 4s^1$ and $\text{Cu}$ ($Z=29$): $[\text{Ar}]\,3d^{10} 4s^1$.

keyFormulas.label: Spin-Only Magnetic Moment & Orbital Angular Momentum
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Count unpaired d-electrons (watch 4s removal first in transition ions!) and compute BM.

wbjeebTraps: Transition-metal ion trap: when ionizing $\text{Fe}$ ($[\text{Ar}]3d^6 4s^2$) to $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, remove $4s$ electrons FIRST $\to [\text{Ar}]3d^6$ ($4$ unpaired $e^-$, NOT $[\text{Ar}]3d^4 4s^2$!).
Remember $\text{Cr}$ ($3d^5 4s^1$, $6$ unpaired $e^-$ in total!) and $\text{Cu}$ ($3d^{10} 4s^1$, $1$ unpaired $e^-$).
Bohr formulas apply ONLY to 1-electron species ($\text{H}, \text{He}^+, \text{Li}^{2+}$), NOT neutral $\text{He}$ or $\text{Li}^+$.
